Education Signaling

When skill cannot be shown directly, a diploma speaks instead.

Studying is easier for the able worker. So only the able can afford the costly degree. For the less able, copying is just too painful. Firms read the diploma and guess the skill. Yet the education itself builds no skill. So the signaling cost below is pure waste.

For example, a fast 🧑 runner easily wins a race medal. A slow runner can hardly win one at all. So a medal tells everyone who is fast. But winning the medal makes nobody faster.

Examples & Exercises

Two types with productivity θH=2\theta_H = 2θH​=2, θL=1\theta_L = 1θL​=1, and education cost c(e,θ)=e/θc(e, \theta) = e/\thetac(e,θ)=e/θ.

When firms believe e≥1e \ge 1e≥1 signals high (wage 222) and e<1e < 1e<1 signals low (wage 111), verify with both types' incentive constraints that e∗=1e^* = 1e∗=1 is the least-cost separating equilibrium.

UH(e)=w(e)−e2,UL(e)=w(e)−eU_H(e) = w(e) - \frac{e}{2}, \qquad U_L(e) = w(e) - eUH​(e)=w(e)−2e​,UL​(e)=w(e)−e
w(e)={2e≥11e<1w(e) = \begin{cases} 2 & e \ge 1 \\ 1 & e < 1 \end{cases}w(e)={21​e≥1e<1​
Show proof

  1. At e∗=1e^* = 1e∗=1 the high type's payoff is UH(1)=2−1/2=1.5U_H(1) = 2 - 1/2 = 1.5UH​(1)=2−1/2=1.5. Deviating to e=0e = 0e=0 earns wage 111 for a payoff of 111, so with 1.5>11.5 > 11.5>1 there is no deviation — the high type's participation constraint (e∗≤2e^* \le 2e∗≤2) holds.

  2. The low type's payoff is UL(1)=2−1=1U_L(1) = 2 - 1 = 1UL​(1)=2−1=1.

    Choosing e=0e = 0e=0 also gives 1−0=11 - 0 = 11−0=1, so there is no gain from mimicking — the low type's incentive constraint (e∗≥1e^* \ge 1e∗≥1) holds with equality.

    That is why this is the least-cost equilibrium: any lower eee would bring the low type along.

  3. The signaling cost borne by the high type is e∗/θH=0.5e^*/\theta_H = 0.5e∗/θH​=0.5 — pure waste, burned only to earn the wage 222 while contributing nothing to productivity.

In the same model, explain through the low type's mimicking incentive why e=0.5e = 0.5e=0.5 cannot be a separating-equilibrium education level.

UL(0.5)=1−0.5=0.5,UL(1)=2−1=1U_L(0.5) = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5, \qquad U_L(1) = 2 - 1 = 1UL​(0.5)=1−0.5=0.5,UL​(1)=2−1=1
Show proof

  1. At e=0.5e = 0.5e=0.5 the wage is 111, so the low type's payoff is UL(0.5)=1−0.5=0.5U_L(0.5) = 1 - 0.5 = 0.5UL​(0.5)=1−0.5=0.5. But choosing e=1e = 1e=1 earns the wage 222 for a payoff of UL(1)=2−1=1>0.5U_L(1) = 2 - 1 = 1 > 0.5UL​(1)=2−1=1>0.5.

  2. So the low type strictly gains from mimicking, and e=0.5e = 0.5e=0.5 cannot separate the types. Separation requires the low type's incentive constraint 2−e∗≤12 - e^* \le 12−e∗≤1, i.e. e∗≥θL(θH−θL)=1e^* \ge \theta_L(\theta_H - \theta_L) = 1e∗≥θL​(θH​−θL​)=1.
